---
title: "Generator"
---

The current generator is a Python CLI with a small `questionary` interactive layer. Template rendering still uses the standard library `string.Template` so the downstream repository contract can stabilize before introducing a heavier renderer such as Banks or Cookiecutter.

## Commands

List available templates:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar list-templates
```

List available model profiles:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar list-model-profiles
```

List available advisory profiles, tool profiles, and skills:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar list-tool-profiles
uv run python -m repo_familiar list-memory-profiles
uv run python -m repo_familiar list-prompt-profiles
uv run python -m repo_familiar list-safety-profiles
uv run python -m repo_familiar list-privacy-profiles
uv run python -m repo_familiar list-repomap-profiles
uv run python -m repo_familiar list-sandbox-profiles
uv run python -m repo_familiar list-secrets-profiles
uv run python -m repo_familiar list-design-profiles
uv run python -m repo_familiar list-worktree-profiles
uv run python -m repo_familiar list-skills
```

Check generated assets against bootstrap metadata:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar check --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar check --path /path/to/repo --format json
```

Classify generated asset changes for possible upstream contribution:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar diff-upstream-candidate --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar diff-upstream-candidate --path /path/to/repo --format json
```

Preview upgrade readiness without writing files:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar upgrade --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar upgrade --path /path/to/repo --format json
```

Get recommendations for an existing repository before bootstrapping:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar advise --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar advise --path /path/to/repo --format json
```

Preview generation without writing files:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar generate \
  --name "Demo Project" \
  --description "A generated demo." \
  --output /tmp/demo-project \
  --agent-harness opencode \
  --model-profile default-coding \
  --tool-profile cq \
  --memory-profile memory-local \
  --secrets-profile dotenv-local \
  --skill cq \
  --skill session-focus \
  --skill grill-with-docs \
  --dry-run
```

Generate a project:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar generate \
  --name "Demo Project" \
  --description "A generated demo." \
  --output /tmp/demo-project \
  --agent-harness opencode \
  --model-profile default-coding \
  --tool-profile cq \
  --memory-profile memory-local \
  --secrets-profile dotenv-local \
  --skill cq \
  --skill session-focus \
  --skill grill-with-docs
```

Generate a project interactively:

```bash
uv sync
uv run python -m repo_familiar generate --interactive
```

The interactive path imports `questionary` lazily. `uv sync` installs the package and its interactive dependency.

Audit an existing repository:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar audit --path /path/to/repo
uv run python -m repo_familiar audit --path /path/to/repo --format json
uv run python -m repo_familiar audit --path /path/to/repo --asset-group docs
```

Preview existing repository bootstrap:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar bootstrap-existing --path /path/to/repo
```

Apply missing assets to an existing repository:

```bash
uv run python -m repo_familiar bootstrap-existing --path /path/to/repo --apply
```

Prompt for existing repository bootstrap options:

```bash
uv sync
uv run python -m repo_familiar bootstrap-existing --interactive
```

## Safety Behavior

The generator refuses to write into a non-empty output directory unless `--force` is passed. This prevents accidental overwrites while templates are still evolving.

Use `--force` only when regenerating known generated output, such as an example snapshot.

Existing repository bootstrap should build on the same safety posture: audit first, dry-run by default, and require explicit action for conflicts or replacements.

When bootstrapping an existing repository, `.repo-familiar/bootstrap.yml` records `bootstrap_mode: existing_repository` and the assets actually written by that operation. Conflicts skipped for safety are not claimed as generated assets.

Use `--asset-group` with `audit` or `bootstrap-existing` for scoped adoption. Supported groups are `agent`, `config`, `design`, `docs`, `memory`, `metadata`, `models`, `plan`, `privacy`, `prompts`, `repomap`, `safety`, `sandbox`, `secrets`, `skills`, `tools`, and `worktrees`.

Generated asset records include `content_sha256` for drift detection. The metadata file itself is presence-checked but not self-hashed.

`diff-upstream-candidate` is read-only. It classifies recorded generated assets as unchanged, modified, missing, or unchecked and adds a recommendation such as `review-for-upstream-improvement`, `review-profile-improvement`, `review-private-or-local-only`, or `restore-generated-asset`. Current Reference Source comparison is advisory; template-variable-heavy assets may report `reference-may-have-changed` until Bootstrap Metadata records richer template context.

`upgrade` is read-only in the current implementation. It reports assets that would need user review, assets that block a future write-capable upgrade, and assets that are unavailable for upgrade. It deliberately reports no safe auto-apply path until Bootstrap Metadata records enough template context for exact rendered comparisons.

## Generated Files

The `basic` template currently writes:

- `.gitignore`
- `README.md`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `.agents/models.yml`
- `.agents/tools.yml`
- `.agents/memory.yml`
- `.agents/prompts.yml`
- `.agents/safety.yml`
- `.agents/privacy.yml`
- `.agents/repomap.yml`
- `.agents/sandbox.yml`
- `.agents/secrets.yml`
- `.env.example`
- `.agents/skill-sources.yml`
- `.agents/design.yml`
- `.agents/worktrees.yml`
- selected skill directories under `.agents/skills/`, including bundled support files when a skill has them
- `docs/_quarto.yml`
- `docs/index.qmd`
- `docs/usage.qmd`
- `docs/architecture.qmd`
- `plan.md`
- `.repo-familiar/bootstrap.yml`
